articles.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Showrunners Address Your Biggest Finale Burning Questions
articles.summary: Avatar: Seven Havens: We talk with show co-creator Michael Dante DiMartino and showrunners Sehaj Sethi and Ethan Spaulding about the current season and beyond.
body: The first Book of Avatar: Seven Havens is, er, in the books with this week’s finale, “The Root Chakra.” And while the final four episodes answered a number of big questions, they raised a ton more — not just about what to expect in Season 2 of the Paramount+ animated series, but Seasons 3, 4, and perhaps beyond. It’s a good thing, then, that we have show co-creator Michael Dante DiMartino and showrunners Sehaj Sethi and Ethan Spaulding on hand to answer all your burning questions.

…Or at least, answer what they can. While we got to see Pavi (Saheli Khan) step up as the Avatar in the finale, unlock her Root Chakra, and head off on a classic Avatar journey to the Floating Isles next season, Nisha (Aishu Devan) — surprisingly — was not part of that unlocking and is staying (for now) in the Haven of Ellora. Not only that, but we also saw Nisha was at least in part the cause of the Fear Anomaly that’s been attacking Ellora all season long, activated when her parents abandoned her; as a side effect, she accidentally killed her parents in a rock slide.
points: Avatar: Seven Havens: We talk with show co-creator Michael Dante DiMartino and showrunners Sehaj Sethi and Ethan Spaulding about the current season and beyond.

articles.title: Nintendo Reveals Surprise Pikmin Day Direct
articles.summary: Nintendo has revealed a surprise Nintendo Direct for Pikmin Day because it has apparently decided that's a thing now.
body: Instead of spooky game announcements or horror movie memes, video game fans woke up to on Halloween 2026 was Mario creator Shigeru Miyamoto's face. That's because Nintendo has declared November 1 as Pikmin Day, and it's got a brand-new Direct to celebrate the occasion.

Yes, really. None of this is a joke. There's a little more than nine minutes of announcements to go over. Although there's no Pikmin 5 reveal or anything else too groundbreaking here, Miyamoto did take the time to share new information about Pikmin 4 and promised that, "going forward, I want people to know more about Pikmin."

So, to start, why is the first of November Pikmin Day? Nintendo's miniaturized franchise launched in Japan in October 2001 before coming to North America in December, so there's no tie to a release date like you might have guessed. Instead, Miyamoto explained that November 1 is Pikmin Day because there were originally only three Pikmin, which, when standing next to each other, kinda looks like "11.1."

articles.title: Phantom Blade Zero Just Killed Crimson Desert's Chances At a GOTY
articles.summary: Phantom Blade Zero is off to a roaring start. The Wuxia action game by S-Game started the week with strong reviews and ended it with stratospheric player numbers on Steam, where the Chinese audience can be relied upon to turn out for a big release from their native country.
body: Phantom Blade Zero is part of a new wave of Unreal Engine 5-powered, AAA PC and console games from China. The figurehead of this wave was Black Myth: Wukong, 2024's Soulslike-adjacent riff on Journey to the West by Game Science, which went on to a Game of the Year nomination at The Game Awards. It looks like that will be Phantom Blade Zero 's fate, too.

There's a pretty direct comparison between the two games. Along with this year's Crimson Desert and, arguably, Blood of the Dawnwalker, they are what I call " outsider AAA ": ambitious productions from outside the big publisher system looking to take it on at its own game. Often made in Central Europe or East Asia, these games present themselves as old-school "gamer's games" with an uncompromising aesthetic and design direction that's both back-to-basics and no-holds-barred. They can garner passionate support from a certain breed of reactionary gamer, but also reach a broad general audience with their lush visuals and technical prowess.
points: Phantom Blade Zero is off to a roaring start.

articles.title: Activision to remove Itaewon crowd crush footage from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 and apologises to victims' families
articles.summary: Activision has apologised to the bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it will remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.
body: In a new statement reported by Inven Global, Activision said the footage "will be completely removed" via a game update scheduled to roll out on 12th November.
The statement was issued in Korean, and the quotes come via Inven Global's AI-assisted, editor-reviewed translation.

As we reported earlier this week, the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died. The bereaved families' association and the Citizens Countermeasure Meeting called for its removal.
"We bow our heads in deep sympathy and apology to the bereaved families and victims who were deeply hurt by this incident, as well as to everyone we have caused concern," Activision said.

articles.title: Skyblivion's Biggest Legal Challenge Yet Is Not Coming From Bethesda
articles.summary: Skyblivion, an ambitious mod aiming to recreate all of The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion within Skyrim's game engine, has run into a new legal challenge after over a decade of volunteer-driven development.
body: On Oct. 30, the Skyblivion team took to X and YouTube to explain that a former volunteer on the project is attempting to sue the others working on it. That unnamed volunteer allegedly took issues with the team's "decompilation of parts of their work" after they left, although those still working on Skyblivion believed that this was necessary to "maintain functionality and fix issues in systems already built into the project after access to the original source code repository was revoked."

As Skyblivion neared completion, the legal threats escalated, and they even demanded the real names and addresses of others working on the project. While the code under dispute was ultimately removed from Skyblivion by those still on the project, that former volunteer is still pursuing legal action. As such, the remaining modders decided to update fans on the situation and even ask if any of them would want to volunteer their legal skills to help address this.

articles.title: The Mortuary Assistant dev on laying his cancelled Paranormal Activity game to rest, resurrecting it as a Halloween freebie, and a potential return to his biggest game
articles.summary: Halloween feels like an especially appropriate time for Playable Archive's arrival. It's a genuinely spooky found-footage affair for one - a cleverly orchestrated 30-or-so minutes of scares from the developer of horror hit The Mortuary Assistant, released this week as a Halloween freebie.
body: For Clarke, Paranormal Activity was a good fit for his preferred story-first approach to horror: one less about cinematic scares that seize control of the camera, and more about "passive" chills; moments where something happens which might not be obvious, and which many players might even miss, giving them slightly different experiences they'll have fun sharing. "I think the flavour I like to do," he explains, "is something that feels like you're driving the experience as opposed to me just putting you on rails and showing you."

And the project felt like an opportunity to add depth to a series that so far hasn't delved much further than spooky houses and demonic possession, in a way Clarke particularly enjoys. "I love lore - demonic lore was a big thing in The Mortuary Assistant - [and so] I built a whole demonology for Paranormal Activity, and built out this whole new concept that still tied in with everything from the films," he recalls. "I was really excited to do this deeper thing... that maybe could be used for other things in the future, other games, films, you know."

articles.title: 'No Man's Sky' Players Pay Homage To Star Trek's Patrick Stewart
articles.summary: Patrick Stewart was a celebrated actor whose career spanned decades of film, television, and theater. He became a household name playing Professor Charles Xavier in the X-Men films, but his work also included decades of live performances with the Royal Shakespeare Company and memorable roles as…
body: Now, players of No Man's Sky are finding a fitting way to honor the late actor, who died this week at the age of 86. Across the game's vast universe, fans have begun naming planets and entire star systems after Stewart, creating virtual memorials that celebrate his life and career.

The tributes began gaining traction on Reddit, where one player called on the community to name a planet in their current star system after Stewart, wherever they happened to be exploring. The post urged players to “spread his name across the No Man's Sky universe.” It closed with a line that should sound familiar to any Star Trek fan: “Make it so.”

The idea has caught on, with the post collecting around 1,900 upvotes and players sharing the planets and memorials they've created. One player named a planet “Picard's Rest” and placed a small cross beside a communication beacon bearing the inscription “Sir Patrick Stewart 1940-2026.” They also shared the planet's coordinates, so other players could visit and pay their respects.

articles.title: Austin Abrams Was Grabbed by Tentacles in a 35-Foot Whale Head for the Thriller ‘Whalefall’
articles.summary: “It was super important that Austin felt like he was in these environments and his body had to respond to them,” Avery told Polygon in a virtual interview. “All that motion on camera is motion that we’re making. It’s not animated. That means Austin’s body is responding to real action in real time.”
body: In Brian Duffield’s adaptation of Daniel Kraus ’ survival thriller Whalefall, Jay Gardiner (Austin Abrams) is swallowed by a sperm whale while scuba diving and has to desperately fight to escape its gullet. It’s a wild concept, but Kraus and production designer Ramsey Avery sell it by making Jay’s plight as realistic as possible. That involved building a 35-foot-long whale head and four different stomach sets that could be jostled, climbed, and filled with goop simulating digestive juices.

One set was built on a rig to create a rocking motion, while another was part of a cylinder akin to a washing machine so Austin could be tossed around. Another was constructed on a seesaw so it could be tipped to soak Abrams in methylcellulose, an organic slime that simulated the whale’s stomach acid. Puppets were used for the giant squid that grapples Jay, pulling him into the whale’s mouth.

articles.title: Aliens, Bigfoots, and Monsters… Remembering the Age of the Weirdumentary
articles.summary: In the conspiracy-minded 1970s, monster ‘documentaries’ were a huge hit at the box office.
body: “I think it was people just questioning what the norm was… what is real, what isn't real,” James L. Conway, who worked as a writer/producer/director at Sunn Classic, tells IGN. “There were very few outlets back then to experience these things, very few TV channels. Through a theatrical window, we were able to make movies about these subjects. They were incredibly popular because there was no other place for people to get knowledge about this… no YouTube, no Wikipedia, no social media. If you wanted to see something that was on the unusual side, it was a theatrical motion picture.”

Conway was a college senior at the University of Denver around 1971 when he was in the Mass Communications Department and the phone rang. It was Charles E. Sellier Jr., who ran an industrial film and commercial company in Denver.

Continues Conway, “Chuck was looking for cheap labor to edit his industrial films. I said, ‘I'm your guy.’ While I finished college I worked for Chuck, and after about three months I said to him, ‘You know, I can direct these shows better than the people you're hiring.’ Total chutzpah. He gave me a shot, I did really well, and that began our relationship.”

articles.title: Final Fantasy 14 reveals Evercold’s second new job and February release date, with pre-orders opening next week
articles.summary: Final Fantasy 14 's next expansion, Evercold, will launch on 23rd February 2027, and its second new job is zephyr, a physical ranged DPS that fights with a crossbow and a bird.
body: Producer and director Naoki Yoshida revealed the job during the opening keynote of the Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival 2026 in Tokyo. Zephyr pairs crossbow shots with support from an avian familiar called Nephele, and joins Bastion, the greatshield-wielding tank revealed as Evercold's first new job at Fan Festival Berlin earlier this year.

Pre-orders for Evercold and the previously announced Collector's Box open on Wednesday 4th November at 9am GMT. Anyone who pre-orders gets early access, plus a Wind-Up Köttr minion and Halone's Earring, which boosts EXP from defeating enemies by 30 percent. The in-game items are delivered as soon as you pre-order, so you can use the earring to level jobs before Evercold arrives.

The Collector's Box is physical goods only. It doesn't include the game, in-game items or pre-order bonuses. Inside you'll find an art box featuring an Evercold illustration by Yoshitaka Amano, a figure of the Warrior of Light as a reaper, an Ethos metal keychain, a Köttr mini plush, and a Tapestry of the Fourth.

articles.title: A former volunteer is threatening legal action against fan-made game project Skyblivion
articles.summary: A former volunteer is threatening legal action against Skyblivion, the long-running fan remake of Oblivion built in Skyrim's engine, over code they contributed to the project.
body: The unofficial project, which remakes 2006's The Elder Scrolls 4: Oblivion, is being made by volunteers from the TES Renewal Project, the modding group that also works on Morrowind remake Skywind.

Bethesda has allowed the project to continue on condition that it replaces all of the original game's assets, and the team continued working on it after Bethesda released its own Oblivion Remastered in April 2025.
In a statement posted to Twitter/X on 30th October, the Skyblivion team said that after the volunteer left, the two sides disagreed over the "continued use and maintenance" of their work.

The main issue was the team's decompilation of parts of that code, which it said was needed "to maintain functionality and fix issues" after its access to the original source code repository was revoked.

articles.title: id Software co-director says the Doom developer is 'working more closely with MachineGames than ever' after Xbox laid off 'about half of our studio'
articles.summary: Id Software has tightened its relationship with fellow shooter specialists MachineGames according to studio co-director Marty Stratton, after Xbox laid off roughly half of the Doom developer's employees earlier this year.
body: Stratton was asked how the studio was doing following Xbox's massive job cuts at a recent press event for Doom: The Dark Ages' Revelations DLC (via IGN ) and he was keen to assure everyone that things are hunky dory at the legendary FPS developer.

"We're doing great," Stratton explained. "Not to handwave the [layoffs] away … everybody knows we had about half of our studio exit as part of that. But there was a very deliberate effort to make sure that we were incredibly viable coming out of that across everything we do, across game development and [the] technology department."

As part of its response to those layoffs, id Software has apparently deepened its ties with MachineGames, developers of Wolfenstein: The New Order and, more recently, the excellent Indiana Jones and the Great Circle.

articles.title: How fast do you type, and has playing MMOs improved your typing in any way?
articles.summary: Terminally Online. This is Terminally Online: PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about…
body: Final Fantasy 14 released a new typing minigame recently—you hop on over to the Gold Saucer, you rock up with a party of four, and you compete with each other to see how many waves you can defeat with the literal power of words. It's a fun little laugh, and as someone who types for a living, I spent a couple hours getting all of my rewards from it.

But not everyone has had as much fun as I—someone who has spent arguably too much of their life in front of a keyboard—am having. Typing speeds among MMO players vary greatly, despite it being the predominant form of communication. This became incredibly obvious to me when I sat down and tip-tapped my way through this mode.

Some players, I left in the dust—others I was level-pegging with, and some of them seemed blessed with divine powers of fingerwork (stop giggling) that left me agog. Also some people were just using bots, but hey, not everyone who's faster than me did. Which got me thinking—you, my fellow MMO players. How fast do you type?
If you're not familiar with your own speed, I invite you to go on your WPM tester of choice (there are plenty on Google) and pump some numbers.

articles.title: Anthropic updates Claude to 'steer it away' from letting users clone games following weeks of Steam being inundated with AI slop
articles.summary: Anthropic has updated Claude Opus 5.5 to "steer it away" from letting users clone other developers' games, after weeks of Steam being overrun with AI slop and outcries from the game development community.
body: In an update spotted by X user Chasm (via Game Developer ) Anthropic added a new rule to Claude Code's "Rules". Listed under "tengu_heron_brook", the rule reads, "Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user's own designs and assets. Do not build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original."

The addition was later confirmed by Addy Osmani, a member of Anthropic's technical staff. In a response to Chasm's post, Osmani stated, "We added two sentences to Claude Code's prompt on Opus 5.5 to steer it away from recreating someone else's specific game because using Claude to infringe IP is against our usage policy."

Osmani added that "original games, genre games, and games built from your own design are meant to keep working. We'll continue to iterate to ensure that we're striking the right balance. In the meantime, if Claude turns down something that's yours, send it my way."

Opus 5.5 has proved adept at reverse engineering code, causing all manner of disruption within the games industry. The effects range from rapid decompiling of old console games to the PS5 being jailbroken.

videos.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 - Switch 2 Tech Review - Input Latency, Frame-Rates + Visuals Tested
videos.summary: Digital Foundry is now fully independent! Join the DF Supporter Program and support the team:
body: Can Switch 2 compete with the other consoles? The campaign mode runs at 30fps, and it retains an impressive amount of the COD Engine's features here. Multiplayer is a bigger point of contention though. We have cross-platform online play with PS5 and Xbox machines - and the good news is matches those with a 60fps target here. Input latency is an issue on Switch 2 though, and we've found controller inputs lag behind the PS5 results. Note: latency results in this video relate to multiplayer only.
